question: Who invites the leader of the majority party to form the Government?
solution:
The correct answer is __**President**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The party that wins more seats in the Lok Sabha elections forms the government.
 
• In India, the President invites the Leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha to form the government.
 
• The President appoints this leader as the Prime Minister and the rest of the ministers are appointed by the President on the advice of the Prime Minister.
 
• If **no party** gets a majority, in such a situation, the President can invite a coalition of parties to form the government. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chief Secretary**:

 
 
• The post of **Chief Secretary** (**Mukhya Sachiv**) is the **senior-most position control **within the **civil services **of the **states** and **union territories** of India.
 
• The position is a **cadre post** for the **Indian Administrative Service**. 
 
 
 
• **Chief Justice of India:**​
 
 
• The Chief Justice is responsible for the allocation of work to other judges.
 
• The Chief Justice administers the oath of office to the President In the absence of the President and the Vice-President, the Chief Justice sits as the Acting President of India
 
• The Chief Justice is the ex-officio Chancellor of most autonomous law schools in India.
 
• The individual must be a citizen of India. 
 
• The person must not exceed 65 years of age. 
 
 
 
• **Vice-President:****​**
 
 
• Article 63 of the Indian Constitution states that "There shall be a Vice President of India."
 
• The Vice President acts as President in the absence of the president due to death, resignation, impeachment, or other situations.
 
• The Vice President of India is also **ex officio Chairperson of the Rajya Sabha**.
 
• ​The Vice-President is the second-highest constitutional office in India. ​
